description.purpose: Composite agent: one hive that references session-keeper@2.0.4, collector@3.0.0, dispatcher@1.1.0 and summarizer@2.0.1 as sub-units plus an llm brain slot, with every internal edge pre-wired -- the stamp promotion, the seam into the brain, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback with restore_ttl and its iteration bound, the close path, the write fan-out and the system.handover return. The topology the Egon rollout wired by hand, as one add_nodes. Since 4.2.0 (GH #55) two more internal edges belong to it: the two tools this composite IMPLEMENTS -- memory_recall and thread_recall, both answered by the collector inside it -- are routed from the dispatcher to the collector by this template's own graph, and the tool exit towards the caller became a guarded default edge (GH #283) that stays silent for exactly the names an ordinary edge already claimed.
description.use_when: Whenever a colony needs a conversational agent that remembers its own session: a chat surface, a phone line, an operator console. Instantiate via add_nodes AND wire the four ports via add_edges IN THE SAME MUTATION - the composite is edge-connected from apply on (no island dance). Instantiation needs ctx.model (a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B).
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells - the tool set is the per-agent choice and its lanes are wired per instance on hop.tool_name. ONE exception since 4.2.0 (GH #55), and it is a boundary rather than a gap: the two tools this composite IMPLEMENTS -- memory_recall and thread_recall, both served by the collector inside it -- are routed by this template's own edges and need no wiring from the parent at all. A tool the composite implements is topology; a tool the parent wires is the agent. No memory hive, no surface proxy, no drain cell, no persona: the write target, the recall port, the reply sink and where errors land are all the parent tree's decision.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the composite's own path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./session-keeper, ./collector, ./dispatcher, ./summarizer, ./brain or ./errors is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route -- the door edges in here decide which cell that means. Ingress: that path, lane in_turn (the parent edge MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, otherwise every chat lands on the channel 'default'). Reply exit: the same path on hop.route=='answer' (THREE sorts: a real answer, a round that hit max_iter told apart by hop.round_capped, and -- since collector@2.1.1 -- a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write, told apart by hop.degraded, which such a message carries INSTEAD of round_capped. A reply edge guarded on round_capped alone lets the third through and reads a store refusal to a person as a real answer, so guard on both; GH #343). Write exit: the same path on hop.route=='write' (the closed session as one batch; the target is the parent's choice), and the same path on hop.route=='turn_write' - ONE finished turn per message and never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11): one user/assistant turn in messages[], hop.turn_id '<session_id>#<index>', hop.turn_index and hop.happened_at beside it, which is the shape a memory hive's episode lane reads, so a memory behind it is fresh per turn. On unless params.turn_write is set to '' or '0'. It is NOT the same target as 'write': that route carries a closed day for whoever archives one, and wiring both into one memory would be a second writer over turns this lane already wrote. Error drain: the same path on hop.route=='error' (MUST be wired). Per instance: the same path on hop.route=='tool' && hop.tool_name=='<name>' out to each tool cell, and every tool cell back into that same path with route in_tool. Optional: the recall / in_bundle pair for a memory hive, in_sweep, and the two operator lanes of the context window, in_prune and in_round_sweep. in_prune is PAIRED (since 3.0.6): it answers unconditionally -- with what it cut or with a zero report saying nothing was eligible -- on hop.route=='prune', and required_drains refuses a mutation that wires the ingress without a plain subscription to the report. RETRACTED in 4.2.0 (GH #55): until 4.1.1 this paragraph told the caller to wire the two tools the composite serves ITSELF -- a loop at the composite's own path, hop.tool_name=='memory_recall' back in on lane in_memory_call and hop.tool_name=='thread_recall' back in on lane in_thread_call. There is NOTHING left to wire for either of them, and a caller that still draws those two edges gets a DOUBLE delivery of every such call, so remove them when you lift an instance to 4.2.0. Both lanes stay declared and stay real doors at that same path -- a caller MAY still hand such a call in on them -- but nothing obliges it to. How the composite answers them is not a caller's address: see description.purpose and the README. The sub-units in here are sealed hives of their own, and for a caller that changes nothing: they are INTERIOR to this composite, which is sealed too, so an endpoint naming one of them -- or reaching past it, as in ./session-keeper/stamp or ./collector/assemble -- is refused with hive_port_boundary all the same. Which cell inside picks a message up is decided by the in_ lane the edge sets, by the door edges in here, and that is what lets the inside of a sub-unit change without touching a caller.

model.because: the model the brain infers with — a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B
